# PDF smoke fixtures

Pinned fixtures for `web/pdf/test/smoke-node.mjs`. Each `*-reference.txt` is
the extracted PDF text (`pdftotext`, run on the host) of a document compiled
**natively** with Tectonic; the browser engine's output must match it
byte for byte (ADR0017/ADR0019 fitness functions). Regenerating a reference
is a deliberate, auditable act: rerun the commands below and diff before
recommitting.

## let-it-be (standalone song, ADR0017)

Generated by `tectonic let-it-be.tex` against the pinned songs pack. The
method documented under "Shared setup" below reproduces the committed
`let-it-be-reference.txt` byte-for-byte (validated 2026-11-01), so one
procedure covers both fixtures.

## demo-book (multi-song book with a title index, ADR0019)

The songs package's index pipeline is a three-step flow that a single TeX
pass cannot complete: LaTeX pass 1 writes `<index>.sxd` data files, the
external `songidx` step converts one into `<index>.sbx`, and a later LaTeX
pass typesets the real index entries. The reference therefore needs two
tectonic invocations with the pinned `songidx.lua` in between — exactly the
sequence the PDF worker reproduces in the browser (engine compile →
`songbook-core::songidx` conversion → engine recompile). The committed
`demo-book-reference.txt` was generated with these commands inside a
throwaway `songbook-devcontainer:latest` container:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace songbook-devcontainer:latest
```

```sh
# inside the container (repo mounted at /workspace)
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y texlive-binaries   # texlua
W=/tmp/native && rm -rf "$W" && mkdir -p "$W/bundle"
tar -xzf /workspace/web/dist/pdf-assets/engine/bundle.tar.gz -C "$W/bundle"
tar -xzf /workspace/web/dist/pdf-assets/pack/pack.tar.gz     -C "$W/bundle"
# tectonic's directory bundle needs a SHA256SUM manifest (and it must not
# list itself): generate it after both extractions.
( cd "$W/bundle" &&
  find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUM | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort |
  xargs sha256sum > /tmp/SHA256SUM.tmp && mv /tmp/SHA256SUM.tmp SHA256SUM )
unzip -p /workspace/web/pdf/.cache/songs.zip songs/songidx/songidx.lua > "$W/songidx.lua"
cd "$W" && cp /workspace/web/pdf/test/fixtures/demo-book.tex .

# step 1: tectonic's internal passes; the index renders the package's
#         placeholder and the run keeps titleidx.sxd
tectonic -b "$W/bundle" -f latex.fmt --keep-intermediates demo-book.tex

# step 2: the external songidx conversion (same interpreter and locale the
#         songidx goldens in crates/songbook-core use)
LC_ALL=C texlua songidx.lua titleidx.sxd titleidx.sbx

# step 3: recompile; this run typesets the real index entries
tectonic -b "$W/bundle" -f latex.fmt --keep-intermediates demo-book.tex
```

then on the host (so the reference is extracted with the same pdftotext the
smoke uses):

```sh
pdftotext <container's demo-book.pdf> web/pdf/test/fixtures/demo-book-reference.txt
```

## Original synthetic tablature fixtures (issue 84e5e08, 2026-11-06)

These inputs were written specifically for this test, not copied from songs or
locally excluded tabs. `tab-fixtures.mjs` drives the **public wasm Session API**:
no candidate tablature LaTeX is handcoded. The smoke regenerates TeX in memory
and requires it to equal the committed exports before compiling those exact
exports through the deployed PDF worker.

- `synthetic-tabs.txt` → `synthetic-tabs.tex`: three retained six-string
  blocks mixed with chord-only, verse, chorus and outro material. The first
  block has six **56-column** ASCII rows, including two leading/trailing
  spaces, two-/three-cell interior gaps, two-digit frets, slides, and literal
  hostile-looking `\end{songs}%\input{never-read}` plus TeX punctuation.
  Apostrophe/backtick exercise cmtt slots 13/18. Alternate labels are opaque;
  consecutive choruses differ only in tab rows and must both survive.
- `synthetic-accompaniment.txt`: original pure chord/lyric material without
  tabs, first in the book. Existing let-it-be/demo-book fixtures and native
  references remain unchanged; both were recompiled and compared with `cmp`.
- `synthetic-partial-tabs.txt`: originally **six** rows. The generator actually
  navigates to and discards the G row (`G|--23--  33--|`), then bulk-accepts
  the remaining material and transposes chords by +2. The five original
  retained rows are unchanged; core emits the partial/source-line note and
  unchanged-tab warning. No missing string is invented.
- `synthetic-tab-book.tex`: core `composeBook` combines accompaniment,
  complete tabs, and the reviewed partial song, with a real title index.

### Original synthetic annotated/split fixtures (2026-11-09)

`synthetic-annotated-tabs.txt` adds a separate original study; it does not
change the four earlier smoke fixtures or their references. Its literal order
is an arbitrary performance comment, a parenthetical chord cue, a heading
with the alternative connector `or`, then exactly six string rows. Ordinary
chord/lyric material follows the group and remains ordinary material.

`annotated-tab-fixtures.mjs` loads the actual optimized wasm glue and drives
`SongbookSession`, rather than fabricating TeX:

- Verify automatic cue → heading → six-string recognition, exact leading,
  interior and trailing spaces, annotation/string roles and camelCase provenance.
- Navigate to and explicitly `handleAction("tab_annotation")` the adjacent
  arbitrary comment. Only that selected row changes; all nine associated rows
  still contain exactly six strings, with no partial/unsupported warning.
- Export `synthetic-annotated-tabs.tex` through core (one Letter page).
- Call `planTabSplit(22)`; check three annotation previews and six string
  previews, raw-column fragments, padding, provenance and non-repeated text.
  Cancel must be non-mutating; Apply consumes a private one-use plan.
- Apply and export `synthetic-annotated-tabs-split.tex` (one Letter page):
  three left annotation fragments + six left strings, then three right
  annotation fragments + six right strings. Annotation text is cut once,
  not copied in full above both children. One Undo restores the initial
  annotated group; reapply and bulk Keep preserve the same split export.
- Use core `composeBook` for `synthetic-annotated-tab-book.tex` (four Letter
  pages: title, real songidx index, accompaniment, split annotated study).
  Both standalone body/bookParts and ordinary D/A chord catalogue are checked;
  annotation chords are not added to that catalogue.

All three TeX files and both reference extractions per file are generated by
the commands below. Native Tectonic uses the unchanged pinned engine bundle,
pack, and (for books) `songidx.lua`. The default smoke and deployed helper copy
compile these exact exports through the deployed worker and require byte-exact
native text **and** layout. Physical bounding boxes check 10pt cmtt cell widths,
raw-column indentation, 12pt baselines, annotation/string ordering, and atomic
annotation-plus-six-string groups on a page. A complete-row matcher avoids
confusing an annotation fragment with an ordinary lyric containing that word.

### Regenerate the core exports

Do not run `web/build.sh` on an in-progress dirty integration tree: prepare
current glue manually without removing already-built PDF assets. From the
repository root (the dist `{"type":"module"}` marker must already exist):

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace \
  songbook-devcontainer:latest bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build -p songbook-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release
    wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir web/dist --out-name songbook_wasm \
      target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/songbook_wasm.wasm
    wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int -Oz \
      web/dist/songbook_wasm_bg.wasm \
      -o web/dist/songbook_wasm_bg.wasm
  '
node web/pdf/test/tab-fixtures.mjs web/dist web/pdf/test/fixtures --write
node web/pdf/test/annotated-tab-fixtures.mjs web/dist web/pdf/test/fixtures --write
# --check is the default and rejects any stale export without writing it.
node web/pdf/test/tab-fixtures.mjs web/dist web/pdf/test/fixtures --check
node web/pdf/test/annotated-tab-fixtures.mjs web/dist web/pdf/test/fixtures --check
```

### Regenerate actual native PDFs and references

`regenerate-native-tabs.sh` verifies the existing pinned bundle, pack and
songs.zip hashes, extracts **bundle then pack**, builds the directory-bundle
SHA256SUM manifest, and runs native Tectonic (`-f latex.fmt`). For the book it
runs Tectonic → pinned `songidx.lua` under `LC_ALL=C texlua` → Tectonic.
Fresh per-fixture directories avoid stale indexes. No browser output is ever
used to manufacture a native reference.

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/opencode/tab-integration
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace \
  -v /tmp/opencode/tab-integration:/tmp/opencode/tab-integration \
  -w /workspace songbook-devcontainer:latest bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y texlive-binaries
    bash web/pdf/test/regenerate-native-tabs.sh /tmp/opencode/tab-integration/native
  '

# Host extraction uses the same pdftotext as the host smoke.
set -euo pipefail
for name in synthetic-tabs synthetic-tab-book \
  synthetic-annotated-tabs synthetic-annotated-tabs-split synthetic-annotated-tab-book; do
  pdf="/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/native/$name/$name.pdf"
  pdftotext "$pdf" "web/pdf/test/fixtures/$name-reference.txt"
  pdftotext -layout "$pdf" "web/pdf/test/fixtures/$name-layout-reference.txt"
  pdftoppm -png -r 110 "$pdf" "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/$name-native"
done
git diff -- web/pdf/test/fixtures
```

### Verification and extraction caveats

```sh
# Required default asset build + smoke inside the devcontainer, with current
# glue already prepared. No SMOKE_TEST override.
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace \
  songbook-devcontainer:latest bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; bash web/build-pdf-assets.sh'
# Separate full host smoke: deployed helpers + worker + fixtures are all used.
set -euo pipefail
PDF_SMOKE_OUT=/tmp/opencode/tab-integration \
  node web/dist/pdf-assets/test/smoke-node.mjs web/dist/pdf-assets web/dist/pdf-assets/test/fixtures
```

Both default and `-layout` extractions must match the actual native references
**exactly**, including final LF/form feeds; no trimming/normalization is used
for parity. Poppler may collapse or miscount repeated spaces (even losing a
dash in default extraction's reading-order heuristic). Consequently the smoke
also decodes the generated numeric glyph/measured-space tokens back to the
complete source rows, then checks actual `pdftotext -bbox-layout` word
coordinates: every glyph in order, gaps in fixed cmtt cells, 12pt baselines,
all rows of each retained block on one page, and meaningful lyric/tab order.
This supplements rather than replaces the exact native comparisons.

The worker is disposed/reinitialized between reference fixtures, matching the
fresh native processes. An observed warm-engine run after demo-book changed
only the default extractor's title/number order (font-subset bounding boxes);
layout text and tab coordinates remained correct. Cross-document warm-engine
plain-text order is not covered by these fresh-process references.

The pinned cmtt10 TFM/PFB are present. kpathsea probes the optional Omega
`cmtt10.ofm` and `cmtt10.ofm.ofm` first; the worker currently reports these two
as missing despite successful TFM-backed output. The smoke logs/permits only
those exact optional probes and rejects every other missing input. Production
worker normalization is unchanged.

Reviewed native/browser layout: standalone **2 Letter pages**; book **5 Letter
pages** (title, sorted index, accompaniment, and two tab/mixed pages). Blocks
are atomic: the distinct second chorus begins on standalone page 2/book page
5, and the five-string partial block and its notes fit on book page 5. The
56-cell block has aligned starts/end bars, straight quotes, no visible-space
symbols, wrapping or clipping. The document class currently selects Letter
despite the engine's `paper: "a4"` request; this fixture does not add PDF options.
All seven native/worker page PNGs were also byte-identical at 110 dpi after
rasterization with the same host `pdftoppm`. To repeat that secondary check
(after the host smoke has written its worker PDFs):

```sh
set -euo pipefail
for name in synthetic-tabs synthetic-tab-book \
  synthetic-annotated-tabs synthetic-annotated-tabs-split synthetic-annotated-tab-book; do
  pdftoppm -png -r 110 "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/$name-worker.pdf" \
    "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/$name-worker"
  count=$(pdfinfo "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/native/$name/$name.pdf" |
    awk '/^Pages:/ { print $2 }')
  for ((page=1; page<=count; page++)); do
    cmp "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/$name-native-$page.png" \
      "/tmp/opencode/tab-integration/$name-worker-$page.png"
  done
done
```

Visual checks are not a substitute for the owner's print-layout acceptance.

## Shared setup notes

- **TeX inputs**: the compile uses the engine's own pinned bundle
  (`engine/bundle.tar.gz`, which carries the prebuilt `latex.fmt`) plus the
  pinned pack (`pack/pack.tar.gz`) extracted **over** it, mirroring the
  browser engine's `addFiles` order (bundle first, pack wins — 25 of the 38
  overlapping BaKoMa font files differ between the two). `-f latex.fmt` is
  required because the bundle stores the format prebuilt under that name;
  plain `-f latex` makes native tectonic try to generate a format from a
  `tectonic-format-latex.tex` file this bundle does not carry.
- **Interpreter**: `texlua` (LuaTeX 1.15.0, TeX Live 2022 as packaged in
  Debian 12) — the interpreter the songs package documentation prescribes,
  which supplies the `unicode.utf8` library `songidx.lua` depends on.
- **Locale**: `LC_ALL=C`, so songidx's `strcoll` comparisons are plain byte
  order — the same order the `songbook-core::songidx` port hard-codes.
- **Keeping intermediates**: `--keep-intermediates` leaves `titleidx.sxd`
  (and `demo-book.sxc`) next to the source after step 1; step 3 rewrites the
  same `.sxd` (the index data does not depend on the typeset pages).

## demo-book-reference.txt stats (as committed 2026-11-01)

- 1016 bytes, 4 pages (title, index, 2 song pages), LF line endings.
- Page 2 is the real sorted index (`Every Construct` before `Let It Be`),
  not the package's "Index not yet generated" placeholder.
